title: Choose the visual world for MeTube
question: The roll assigned the Contact Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Contact Sheet
options.lineage: darkroom contact sheets, film edge printing and china-marker proofing
options.thesis: Every download is a strip of film printed onto one proof sheet, developing in the tray and then marked up in grease pencil.
options.viewport: A black film rebate for a navbar with the live counts as amber edge-print, the URL bar as the one bright exposure, and the Downloading, Completed and Subscriptions sections as strips with frame-numbered edges.
options.risk: Film furniture turns into costume if the sprockets and edge print ever outweigh the rows; it has to stay a quiet rebate beside dense data.

raised.raise: Every download carries a stable frame number in its rebate: the index you scan and select by.
State lives in the strip itself: unexposed while queued, latent while developing, light-struck red when it failed; badges only confirm it.
A collapsed section folds to one packet strip that still reports its counts and the live progress.
One exposure legend, used identically in the navbar, the section edges and the rows.

options.label: Dubbing Deck
options.lineage: 1980s double-cassette dubbing decks and reel-to-reel recorders
options.thesis: MeTube as the recorder on the rack: the URL bar is the source, each download a tape in the transport with a tape counter and VU progress.
options.viewport: A faceplate strip holding the URL input and a lit REC-style Download key, with transports for active downloads and the history as a shelf of labelled tapes.
options.risk: The most familiar retro-audio skeuomorph there is; a faceplate is a desk object and loses its logic on a phone.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscopes on an electronics bench
options.thesis: Every active download is a channel on the scope: its real throughput drawn as a trace, speed and ETA on seven-segment readouts.
options.viewport: A graticule band where each running download traces its speed live, readouts beside it, and the history as a measured log beneath.
options.case: Wins on audience: homelab owners read instruments daily and the trace is real data. Loses on clarity for a 2,000-row history, and near-black with neon is the look this category's generated UIs default to.
options.risk: Light mode has no native form; phosphor on black cannot carry the light theme you require.

options.label: Annual Plate Section
options.lineage: design annuals printed on uncoated stock
options.thesis: The downloads as a printed plate section: a strict hairline grid, one grotesque, mono labels and registration marks at every corner.
options.viewport: A sticky mono token bar, the URL field as a plate caption, and the tables as a hairline-ruled plate index.
options.case: Wins on clarity: hairline grids are ideal for dense tables. Loses on audience: a self-hoster has never held a design annual.
options.risk: So restrained it can read as the neutral admin look you already have.

options.label: Depot Destination Blind
options.thesis: Status as cloth courses stepping under a fixed window.
options.viewport: Each download a course stepping through its states.
options.case: One-size condensed caps cannot carry thousands of long titles, and the audience has no tie to depot blinds.
options.kept: State carried by the material itself, not only a label.
options.risk: Reads as a themed poster rather than a tool.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every artifact given a catalog number, state spoken in colour code.
options.viewport: A catalog index navigated by number.
options.case: Coding state instead of labelling it breaks the at-a-glance principle.
options.kept: A stable sequential number as each item's identity.

options.label: Miura-fold Sheet
options.thesis: A packet that unfolds into a full sheet.
options.case: No tie to the audience and no gain in clarity.
options.kept: Every section has a compact packet form and a deployed form.

options.label: Gravity-rain Garden
options.thesis: Colour-coded rain falling toward its own gravity.
options.case: Loses on both axes for a download manager.
options.kept: One legend held level while everything else moves.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The self-hosted app UI played straight, the way Sonarr, Jellyfin or qBittorrent's newer skins look, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: The page you have now, refined: neutral surfaces, a blue primary, clean dense tables.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other self-hosted app, by design.
